message: No detected input validation: The code reads CSV files directly with pd.read_csv() and converts to numpy arrays without any schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards.

No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from local CSV files only; there is no remote fetching, and therefore no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks are implemented.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: CSV files are loaded directly via pd.read_csv with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious samples performed on the data.

No detected model integrity verification: The code trains models from scratch (DecisionTreeClassifier, KNeighborsClassifier, SVC) and never loads pretrained/serialized model weights, so no integrity verification is implemented or needed, but none is present.
No detected label distribution validation: The code reads CSVs and proceeds directly to train_test_split and model fitting without any class balance check or expected-label-set validation.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no activation-pattern analysis, trigger detection, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD) is imported or used; standard scikit-learn classifiers are trained without any privacy mechanisms.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, etc.) or attack methods (FGSM, PGD) are imported or used anywhere in the evaluation code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While train_test_split is used to separate data, the split is done inline with no fixed random seed, no hashing/signing of evaluation data, and cross-validation is performed on the training set only — there is no strong isolation or integrity protection of the held-out test set.
No detected input sanitization: The code reads CSV files directly and passes numpy arrays to models without any shape, range, type, or schema validation on the input data.
No detected output bounds checks: Model predictions and F1/CV scores are printed and returned directly with no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or threshold validation on outputs.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The models used are classical ML classifiers (KNN, Decision Tree, SVM), not LLMs, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
